searchText: Hey all, I was looking at EIP-1559 yesterday and was trying to understand incentives for miners and users. Am I right in understanding that the reason miners don't simply fill every block to maximise tips is because the tip may be lower than the expected loss from processing an additional transaction? Which means tips above a certain level are always included and those below won't be? Also presumably this price in gwei can be fairly closely calculated. Filling a block will increase the base fee (which miners don't get) for the *next* block. Also, you have to pay the base fee (which is burned, so this is a real cost) to fill the block with transactions. As far as what the gas premium miners will require, it is based on increased uncle risk as you implied. Estimates floating around are between 1 nanoeth and 5 nanoeth depending on an individual block's value (which can vary based on fees collected for that block). Right but that cost is not paid by the miners. You're saying if the price increases there will be less than 50% of the block worth of transactions willing to pay, losing out on business? Yes. The system is designed so the price will increase until blocks are only half full. Basically, the fee increases until demand for blockspace drops sufficiently. Right, but surely there's a minimum, which is a point where they'd mine empty blocks instead. And just above that is where most users should sit the majority of the time. It'll only go way up in times of sudden increases. A minimum what? Premium? Or base fee? Yeah, gas price Minimum miner tip There is no gas price anymore. 🙂 There is the premium (sometimes incorrectly called "tip"), and there is the base fee. Miners will individually configure a minimum gas premium that they are willing to accept. We expect this to be between 1 nanoeth/gas and 5 nanoeth/gas if miners are rational and our math and estimates are correct. Any transactions below a miners minimum configured premium will simply not be included in any blocks that miner produces. Right, I understand, what I'm saying is, it feels like when basefee prices are fairly stable, most people only have an incentive to set a premium which is only high enough that it offsets the time to process the extra transaction (assuming everyone is setting a minimal premium). Yes, this is exactly correct and expected behavior. Ok cool 🙂 Thanks! Well, offsets uncle risk + epsilon. 🙂 The miners won't include something with a 0 EV. 😉 But +epsilon EV they will if rational. Another question - am I right in assuming miners expected returns overall will drop with EIP-1559 and hence there will be an expected drop in difficulty after the implementation? If so are there any estimates on what the change will be like? Yes to the first, assuming all else is equal. Whether there is a comensurate drop in difficulty depends on whether miners are currently barely profitable or not. If they have some breathing room (which is likely I think) they won't shutdown. Right, that all makes sense. https://twitter.com/petejkim/status/1418242815440609280?s=20 Will answer on Twitter also responded > if, on Ropsten, the miner accepts your 1 gwei priority fee, you put a 1.1 gwei max fee, and the base fee is 7 *wei*, you'll get back 93 wei or 0.000000093 gwei. Shouldn't this be: 1.1 gwei - ( 1gwei + 7 wei) = 0.093 gwei or 930,000,000 wei Ahh, yes! Thanks <@!707508825955237898> - shared on twitter as well 🙂 We're planning one last 1559 coordination call ahead of London Activation (Aug 4) to convene with wallets, dev tooling, and clients. **14:00 UTC (10 ET) July 30 ** This call is optional but encouraged, we'd love to hear from you. Please DM me with your email address to be added to the invite. Add your questions to the agenda 👇 https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/363
